newsitem.title: USA: Mexico silver output up 9 pct in 1996 - Gold Field.
newsitem.headline: Mexico silver output up 9 pct in 1996 - Gold Field.

text.p: Mexico was once again the world's leading silver producer in 1996, accounting for almost 17 percent of global mine production after its output rose almost nine percent to 81 million ounces (2,528 tonnes), Gold Field Mineral Services Ltd said in its 1997 "World Silver Survey" published Wednesday on behalf of Silver Institute.

"Global silver mine production increased for the second consecutive year in 1996 to 493 million ounces (15,320 tonnes), but this was still some way below the record level set in 1990," one of the report's authors, Philip Klapwijk, told analysts in New York.

"As in the past, primary mines were not the principal source of new silver coming onto the market," he said. "Rather it was a wide group of base metal and gold mining operations, where silver is generated as a by-product or co-product, which produced over 83 percent of the total in 1996."

In the U.S., where silver mine output increased modestly last year to 50 million ounces (1,565 tonnes), a strong rise in production from primary silver mines was almost canceled out by falling by-product silver output from gold mines such as the McCoy Cove, where silver output fell by almost five million ounces.
On the other hand, primary U.S. silver mines Candelaria, Sunshine and Lucky Friday all increased output.
The Coeur and Galena mines, resurrected by Silver Valley Resources, in May last year and now operated as a single unit, produced close to 1.7 million ounces in the remaining seven months of the year.
In other parts of the world, silver output in Australia rose by four percent to 33 million ounces (1,020 tonnes) last year.
But silver production from Australia is expected to rise dramatically once the Cannington mine begins operations from the end of 1997.

Cannington has capacity to produce 24 million ounces (750 tonnes) of silver a year, which if achieved, would make it the single biggest silver mine in the world. ((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
